```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
# Add any other libraries here



```


```{r load-data}
rawdata <- read_csv("data/ames.csv")


```

```{r data}

# Preparing data
data <- rawdata %>%
  select(price, area, Year.Built, Yr.Sold, Year.Remod.Add, Bedroom.AbvGr) %>%
  rename(bedrooms = Bedroom.AbvGr) %>%
  mutate(
    Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold = Yr.Sold - Year.Remod.Add,
    Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built = Year.Remod.Add - Year.Built,
    If.Remodelled = case_when(
      Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built == 0 ~ "No",
      Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built > 0 ~ "Yes"
    )
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

options(scipen = 999)

# medans and medians
median_price <- median(data$price)
mean_price <- mean(data$price)
sd_price <- sd(data$price)
median_bedrooms <- median(data$bedrooms)
mean_bedrooms <- mean(data$bedrooms)
median_area <- median(data$area)
mean_area <- mean(data$area)
sd_area <- sd(data$area)



#graphs

# house prices density plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "lightblue",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Density Distribution of House Prices",
    x = "House Price ($)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
      geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_price,
    colour = "red", # median is red!!
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_price,
    colour = "orange", # mean is orange 
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, max(data$price), by = 100000),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# analysis - graph is positively skewed. Mean > Median > Mode
# this means that most house prices are below the mean
# this means that most people earn moderate amounts but a few earn very high incomes

# histogram for bedrooms per house in ames, iowa
ggplot(data, aes(x = bedrooms)) +
  geom_histogram(
    fill = "darkcyan",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_bedrooms,
    colour = "orange", # orange is the mean of data, else is median
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Bedrooms in Houses in Ames, Iowa",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms per House",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# area of different houses
ggplot(data, aes(x = area)) +
  geom_histogram(
    fill = "darkturquoise",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
    geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_area,
    colour = "red", # median is red!!
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_area,
    colour = "orange", # orange is the mean of data, else is median
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Area of Houses in Ames, Iowa",
    x = "Area",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Scatterplot graphs for relationships

# Graph 1: Price vs Area
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = area, y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Area",
    x = "Area",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)


# Graph 2: Price vs Year Built
p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Year.Built, y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Year Built",
    x = "Year Built",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p2)


# Graph 3: Price vs Year Sold
p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(Yr.Sold), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "purple",
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "House Price Distribution by Year Sold",
    x = "Year Sold",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p3)


# Graph 4: Price vs Year Remodelled
p4 <- ggplot(data %>% 
               filter(If.Remodelled == "Yes"),
  aes(x = Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built, 
      y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "orange", 
             size = 2, 
             alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Years Between Building and Remodelling",
    x = "Years Between Building and Remodelling",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p4)

# Graph 5: Price vs No. of  Bedrooms
p5 <- ggplot(data, 
             aes(x = factor(bedrooms), 
                 y = price)
             ) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "yellow", 
               color = "red", 
               alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Number of Bedrooms",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p5)

# area vs number of bedrooms
p6 <- ggplot(data, 
             aes(x = factor(bedrooms), 
                 y = area)
             ) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "pink", 
               color = "red", 
               alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "House Area vs Number of Bedrooms",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms",
    y = "Area"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p6)

# Graph 7: Price vs Years Between Remodelling and Year Sold
p7 <- ggplot(data %>% 
               filter(If.Remodelled == "Yes"),
             aes(x = Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold, 
                 y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "plum", 
             size = 2, 
             alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Years Between Remodelling and Sale",
    x = "Years Between Remodelling and Sale",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p7)

# Graph 8: Comparing if houses have or haven't been remodelled

p8 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = If.Remodelled, 
                 y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkmagenta") +
  labs(
    title = "House Prices: Remodelled vs Not Remodelled",
    x = "Has the House Been Remodelled?",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p8)
```
``` {r stats}
# Correlations calculations
correlations <- data %>%
  summarise(
    Price_Area_Cor = cor(price, area),
    Price_Yr_Built_Cor = cor(price, Year.Built),
    Price_Yr_Sold_Cor = cor(price, Yr.Sold),
    Price_Yr_Remodelled_Cor = cor(price, Year.Remod.Add),
    Price_Bedrooms = cor(price, bedrooms),
    Price_Btwn_Remod_Built_Cor = cor(price, Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built),
    Price_Btwn_Remod_Sale_Cor = cor(price, Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold)
  )

print(correlations)

#other stats
stats <- data %>%
  summarise(
    mean_price,
    median_price,
    sd_price,
    mean_bedrooms,
    median_bedrooms,
    mean_area,
    median_area,
    sd_area
  )

# y-intercept and gradients *key for report*
# The regression analysis shows a ___itive relationship between...

# Price vs Area
summary(lm(price ~ area, data = data))
# gradient = ~111.7, y-intercept = ~13,290, R^2 = ~0.4995

# Price vs Year Built
summary(lm(price ~ Year.Built, data = data))
# gradient = ~1475, y-intercept = ~-2,727,000, R^2 = ~0.3118

# Price vs Year Remodelled
summary(lm(price ~ Year.Remod.Add, data = data))
# gradient = ~2,041, y-intercept = ~3,869,000, R^2 = ~0.2841

```
